SaidiRun a company, not a chat window

A hosted orchestrator you brief like a manager. It stands up departments, writes the plan, delegates to agents scoped to your repos and tools, verifies the result against observable criteria, and brings it back for your approval.

Get Started
What is Saidi?
Your First Run

Runs, not chat sessions

Every task becomes a durable Run with its own thread, its own branch, and one shared context across every agent that touches it. Close the tab — the Run carries on.

How Runs work

Plans with real acceptance criteria

PRIME freezes a checklist of tasks, each with observable criteria and mechanical checks. A task only reaches done when an independent gate says so — not when the agent claims it.

Plans & Tasks

Agents organised into departments

Project agents scoped to one repo, custom agents grouped into departments with a lead that routes work to its team. Each with its own persona, skills, connectors, and tool permissions.

Agents & Departments

Delegation you can audit

The boss holds a small toolbelt — delegate_to_project, run_agent, remember — and every delegation lands in the Run thread with its cost, its model, and its result.

Delegation

Memory that stays in the workspace

Decisions and house style, scoped per workspace, per member, per project and per agent. Config lives in your repos; memory lives in Saidi and is never committed to a client repo.

Memory & Conventions

Reflexes — CRONs with an event trigger

A normalized event bus (run.finished, run.failed, run.needs_approval, webhooks) plus rules with boolean match trees, cooldowns, dedup keys, and approval gates.

Reflexes & Events

Saidi in one loop ​

You only ever talk to PRIME. It writes the plan, hands each task to the right department, relays their questions back to you, and summarises the outcome — you never have to hold the whole graph in your head.

The pieces you will meet ​

Read these in any order — each concept page is self-contained and links to the others.

Plans & Tasks A frozen checklist with observable acceptance criteria, dependencies, and a verification gate per task. Read Verification & Evidence Nothing is done because an agent said so. Criteria are checked mechanically and the evidence is kept. Read Worktrees & Branches Each Run gets its own git worktree, so parallel agents never fight over one working tree. Read Tenancy & Access The workspace boundary: what belongs to whom, and what one member can see of another's work. Read Channels Talk to Saidi from the web app or Telegram; approve, steer and stop Runs from your phone. Before you start ​

Read the guardrails page first

Saidi writes to real repositories. Set the approval mode and the spend limit you are comfortable with before your first autonomous Run — see Approval & Spend Guardrails. Agents never merge and never force-push, but they do commit and push branches.
